notes.bp: Speech arrives incrementally, but written formatting often needs context that has not arrived yet.
notes.wh: Streaming ITN must balance incomplete context, accuracy, adaptation, and latency.
notes.naive: Run a full-context normalizer after the utterance is complete, or use fixed chunks that ignore right context.
notes.ap: Use a pretrained language model with dynamic chunk sizes and controlled right-context during training and inference.
notes.mech: The model changes its available context as speech arrives, using right-context information without abandoning the streaming budget.
notes.math: Sequence decoding maps spoken-form tokens to written-form tokens; latency and accuracy form the deployment tradeoff.
notes.dots: Normalization is a boundary between recognition and usable text, not a cosmetic postprocessing detail.
notes.ww: The paper reports accuracy comparable to non-streaming ITN and better than prior streaming models on Vietnamese data while maintaining low latency.
notes.limits: Vietnamese data, benchmark, and author-reported latency/results limit cross-language and independent deployment claims.

notes.bp: Meeting speech contains overlapping speakers, and diarization and recognition must make decisions from the same mixed observations.
notes.wh: Overlap changes which speaker evidence is reliable; guided source separation can fail at low signal-to-noise ratio.
notes.naive: Use one diarization model and assume separated observations are equally useful for ASR.
notes.ap: Combine overlap-adaptive diarization with ASR-aware observation addition and a cascaded meeting-recognition system.
notes.mech: A hybrid segmentation/clustering diarizer selects its model by overlap, while ASR-aware observations compensate for weak guided separation before recognition.
notes.math: Diarization assigns speaker-time regions; CER and concatenated minimum-permutation CER measure the downstream meeting transcript.
notes.dots: Separation is not an isolated front end: errors in overlap decisions change recognition evidence and speaker attribution together.
notes.ww: The system reports 9.48% CER and 11.56% cpCER and first place in both MISP tracks.
notes.limits: Challenge tracks, meeting conditions, and author-reported ranking limit generalization and independent reproduction.
